newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Trend for Brazil shrs unclear, hinges on funds.
newsitem.headline: Trend for Brazil shrs unclear, hinges on funds.

text.p: Trend for Brazil's stock market remains unclear Wednesday and will largely depend on the behavior of domestic stock funds, equity analysts and traders said.

Share prices tumbled 8.51 percent Tuesday, with the Bovespa index posting its largest single-day drop since January 1995, prompted in a large part by individual investors from local equity funds who decided to take profits.

Those investors, particularly who joined the funds to take advantage of the bolsa's bull run since the beginning of 1997 and were rattled by newspaper headlines over the market's sharp decline in the previous sessions, could continue withdrawing money from the funds.

"The big question is how investors in these retail funds will react today. That is the factor which will determine whether the market will rise or fall," said Luciano Camargo, equity sales manager at ING Barings, Brazil.
Camargo noted, however, that the overall climate appears to be better today after government officials reiterated that Brazil's foreign exchange policy will remain unchanged.

The selling spree, which made the bolsa lose over 14 percent over three sessions, was triggered by fears that the moves by speculators that forced some Asian countries to devalue their currencies could also hit Brazil and prompt the government to devalue its real currency.
Analysts hope that share prices will recover somewhat today after plummeting for three consecutive sessions.
